In this case, the asymmetry is associated with one channel having an unitary steady value while the other will have a different nonlinear refractive index profile. Looking at the transmission characteristics of the device, one observes that it is possible to decrease greatly the critical power or to present regions of multistability depending on which channel the power is pumped. It is concluded that the asymmetry can lead the coupler to operate in a multivalued function of the critical power for certain values of nonlinear parameters.

articleTitle: Microwave power amplifiers fabricated from wide bandgap semiconductor transistors
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The microwave performance of transistors fabricated from SiC and GaN-based semiconductors is described. It is demonstrated that these devices make possible microwave power amplifiers with superior RF power performance compared to devices fabricated from Si or GaAs. Room temperature RF output power on the order of 4 W/mm and 10-12 W/mm with near ideal power-added efficiency is available from 4H-SiC MESFET's and GaN-based HFET's, respectively. These devices are likely to find application in power amplifiers for base station transmitters for cellular telephone systems, HDTV transmitters, power modules for phased-array radars, and other applications. The devices are particularly attractive for applications that require high RF output power and operation at elevated temperature.

articleTitle: On dynamic stability of conformal PML-FDTD for electromagnetic field computations
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We study the dynamic stability of the perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations of electromagnetic scattering problems. This work extends our previous stability analysis of Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical PML's to the case of a conformal PML. Numerical results illustrate the main findings.

articleTitle: Soliton carrier instability as a communication system noise problem
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The soliton pulse and its characteristics are defined. Erbium doped fiber amplifiers (EDFA) noise power spectral density in the fiber is derived. Superposition of amplifier spontaneous emission (ASE) noise on the soliton signal results in a random frequency shift of the soliton carrier (so called Gordon-Haus effect). This frequency shift is solved as a communication system noise problem and the result is used to determine the maximum permissible system length with the presumed BER<10/sup -9/. Possible methods which can suppress the Gordon-Haus effect are listed.

articleTitle: Cloning solitons in a nonlinear medium coherently driven
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Based on the coexistence of a self-induced soliton with a nonlinear Schrodinger soliton we demonstrate soliton cloning in a three-level system interacting with two resonant fields in a nonlinear waveguide. With this new technique is possible to make copies of a soliton from one wavelength to another wavelength.

articleTitle: Gate controlled 2-DEG varactor for VCO applications in microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A novel gate-controlled Schottky diode varactor is introduced. The three terminal varactor is a modulation doped heterostructure of AlGaAs-GaAs with two Schottky contacts, similar to a metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) diode. Schottky metal contacts are made to a two dimensional electron gas (2-DEG). The third, gate, contact is formed from highly doped n/sup +/ GaAs material to allow an open optical window that can be used for optical gating and mixing. Structure capacitance is less than 1 pF and a change of more than 30 percent from the zero bias capacitance is observed with the applied gate voltage. The interdigital structure dimensions can be scaled to cover a wide range of operation in the microwave and millimeter wave regimes.

articleTitle: High dynamic range fiber optic gyroscope demodulation technique based on triangular waveform phase modulation
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This work describes, in an elucidative fashion, a high dynamic range demodulation technique suitable for open-loop Fiber Optic Gyroscope (FOG) application. The proposed technique relies on special features which are achieved when an integrated optic phase modulator is driven by a triangular waveform signal. Such modulation, combined with the zero crossing technique yields detection of Sagnac phase shift with a dynamic range 30 dB above the sinusoidal driven approach. The dynamic range obtained has an upper boundary that is limited by the optical source coherence function. The experimental results obtained using a Sagnac interferometer are in agreement with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Optical encryption for high-bit rate systems using fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A technique for encrypting optical communication signals using fiber Bragg gratings is proposed and demonstrated. The input pulses were converted into two pulses by differential delay imposed by the reflection on two Bragg grating with different spectral response and separated along the fiber. To recover the original pulses, a similar but inverted grating arrangement is used. The principle has been tested with a periodic pulse train of 1.4 GHz repetition rate.

articleTitle: High-frequency CAD-the key to success in wireless communications
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: As wireless applications continue to expand rapidly, there is an increasing awareness of the strategic importance of advanced high-frequency design technology. This is driven by more stringent system specifications and the growing criticality of time-to-market. This paper overviews some of the general issues involved, concentrating at a technical level on device modeling and simulator technology. The future evolution of the CAD industry is also considered briefly.

articleTitle: Ultrafast optical switching in a nonlinear loop mirror (NOLM) constructed from dispersion decreasing fiber (DDF)
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The performance of a nonlinear optical loop mirror (NOLM) device constructed with a dispersion decreasing fiber (DDF) operating in the soliton and quasi-soliton regime is investigated numerically. Results showed that the soliton regime presents best behavior when compared with the quasi-soliton regime. In the quasi-soliton regime, the transmitted pulse presents strong shaping effect, (compression). However in the soliton regime, the transmitted pulses present fewer fluctuations in the time duration with pump power. Our simulations considering four different profiles, linear, hyperbolic, exponential and Gaussian conclude that, in average, the hyperbolic profile gives the lowest pump power for the first, second and third transmission peaks of transmission compared with the other profiles. The Gaussian profile presents the worse behavior. It was also observed that with a proper choice of the dispersion profile we could have a transmitted pulse with no distortion in the soliton regime. For the quasi-soliton regime, strong compression was observed.

articleTitle: An empirical nonlinear MESFET model based on multi-bias measurements
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A successful modeling technique that leads to a highly accurate nonlinear MESFET model is presented. This model is implemented based on accurate device measurements at different bias voltages using an HP8510C network analyzer. The parameters of the most commonly used nonlinear empirical models like Curtice quadratic, Curtice cubic and Statz models are extracted using GASMAP and FETMEX programs. The best model has been determined and tested for DC and AC operation through computer simulation, which gave more accurate results than existing models. Then, it has been successfully applied in the design and realization of a microstrip oscillator at 8.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Dispersion profile studies on twin core directional fiber couplers
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Twin core nonlinear directional coupler that include loss and dispersion index are examined. The inclusion of loss results in increase of critical power of the coupler while the switching characteristics deteriorate. To compensate for this worse behavior, associated to the loss, we have investigated the effect of the dispersion profile decreasing. We have show that appropriate shaping of the dispersion profile is quite effective to recover, almost completely, the original switching behavior associated to the lossless situation. It is concluded that hyperbole dispersion profile is nearly optimum for recovery of the lossless switching behavior.

articleTitle: A circuit-fed, tile-approach configuration for millimeter-wave spatial power combining
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A circuit-fed, spatially combined transmitter array is described for operation at 44 GHz. The array contains 256 elements where each element consists of a MMIC amplifier and a circularly-polarized microstrip patch antenna. The array is constructed using 16-element tile-approach subarrays, Each subarray is a two RF-level (3-D) multi-chip module (MCM) containing integrated microstrip patch antennas. The basic construction of the transmitter array resembles tile-approach phased arrays; however, the implementation has been tailored for the power combining application. The peak performance at 43.5 GHz is: EIRP of 40.6 dBW (11570 watts), effective transmitted power (Peff) of 5.9 watts, DC-to-RF efficiency of 7.3%, and system gain of 35 dB.

articleTitle: "Fiber From The Home"
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Summary form only given. The term "Fibre From The Home" signifies the paradigm shift away from the top-down, "Fiber To The Home" approach by national operators under strict regulation, to the present deregulated, independent new operator, bottom-up, infrastructure approach. The fundamental mechanisms that drive this development are; deregulation (new players, small-scale development), bandwidth need (Internet, new services), and IP (a common service infrastructure). This has given a new need for the fibre technologies (reliable bandwidth), as well as the possibility to start in a small scale, and it has caused entry of new players such as local operators and infrastructure.

articleTitle: On the design of integrated optical adiabatic tapers made by the sol-gel deposition technique
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the different techniques available for fabricating tapered structures based on the sol-gel deposition process. Experimental difficulties are examined and conclusions drawn leading to the best approach for a future device.

articleTitle: Efficient computation of surface fields excited on a dielectric coated circular cylinder
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An efficient method to evaluate the surface fields excited on an electrically large dielectric coated circular cylinder is presented. The efficiency of the method results from the /spl phi/-propagating representation of the Green's function as well as its efficient numerical evaluation along a steepest descent path. Numerical results are presented for current elements mounted on a dielectric coated cylinder and compared with reference solutions.

articleTitle: Nonuniform bandlimited basis functions in the analysis of axisymmetric reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The use of bandlimited sampling-like basis functions on different kinds of nonuniform grids is investigated in conjunction with the Method of Moments (MoM) integral equation solution to the problem of scattering from axially symmetric reflectors. Particular attention is given to the description of the currents near the edge of reflector surface. Supporting numerical examples are provided using a classical reflector.

articleTitle: New techniques for analysis/synthesis of electrically large satellite antennas
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A novel Gaussian beam method, and a hybrid method, are developed for the efficient analysis of large reflector antenna systems, and large planar phased arrays, respectively. Several numerical results illustrating the speed and accuracy of these methods are described in this paper.

articleTitle: 1.3 /spl mu/m strained MQW AlGaInAs and InGaAsP ridge-waveguide lasers-a comparative study
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Strained multiple quantum wells (MQW) AlGaInAs and InGaAsP ridge-guide lasers operating at 1.3 /spl mu/m are fabricated by using the same process. The comparative investigation shows that AlGaInAs lasers present superior performance in relation to InGaAsP lasers. The characteristic temperature T/sub 0/ for the AlGaInAs lasers, /spl sim/100 K, is twice that of the InGaAsP lasers, /spl sim/500 K, resulting in substantially lower threshold currents, /spl sim/34 mA compared to /spl sim/56 mA at 85/spl deg/C. The modulation bandwidth of AlGaInAs lasers is higher than that of the InGaAsP lasers.

articleTitle: Characterization of the optical and electrical spectra of fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The precise characterization of the linewidth and the electrical mode pattern is presented, in this paper, for a stable erbium-doped fiber ring laser that uses two optical filters. The laser linewidth is measured using a Michelson interferometer, confirming its sharp narrowing as consequence of the mode suppression. The laser performance optimization is accomplished by the determination of the matched condition for simultaneous operation of the both optical filters. An estimate of the RIN due to the introduction of the laser in a communication system is also presented.

articleTitle: New analysis and 3D results of microstrip antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In this work, the rectangular microstrip patch antenna and its arrays are analyzed using the Transverse Transmission Line (TTL) method along with the Transmission Line Model. Since the TTL is a full wave method and very much suitable for microwave components study, it gives accurate effective dielectric constant which contributes definitively to obtaining higher precision antenna parameters. For each type of array is calculated the array factor, considering the excitation, phase and the distance between the individual elements as well as the dimensions. Results for the radiation pattern in E and H-plane in 2 and 3D are presented.

articleTitle: Modal analysis of quasi-guided waveguides by the finite element method with spatial transformations
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This work presents an approach for the computation of resonant modes in quasi-guided waveguides by the finite element method. In this approach, a spatial transformation maps a large external domain, surrounding the guide core, onto a smaller domain containing the waveguide region. Only a few modifications of conventional finite element codes are required to apply the spatial transformation scheme, which can be used in the presence of material nonhomogeneities as well as anisotropies. A weakly guiding optical waveguide is analysed by this scheme and the modal solutions are compared to those obtained by the infinite element and the boundary impedance condition techniques.

articleTitle: Simulink/sup TM/ blocks for simulation of light sources
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In this work is shown how to construct blocks to simulate and analyze optical sources using Simulink. The versatility of this software is used to form analisys blocks in the time and frequency domains. Results for LED (FD), Quantum Well (TD) and Fabry Perot (FD) LASERs are shown, and it is possible to change various parameters to obtain new results according to the necessity.

articleTitle: Development of low coherence laser diode for fiber-optic gyroscope
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Broadband sources are the choice for high-performance fiber-optic gyroscopes. These systems rely on expensive broadband sources exhibiting low spectral modulation such as superluminescent diodes and fiber lasers. We present a low-cost alternative using commercial laser diodes. Spectrum broadening is obtained by reducing the laser facet reflectivity and reconstructing the laser cavity with a mirror deposited on the tip of a pigtailed fiber lead. The device fabrication and current experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Design of aperture-coupled microstrip antenna for applications in wireless communications
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In this paper, we describe the design and the experimental implementation of a new aperture-coupled microstrip antenna for broadband applications in wireless systems. Using an aperture-coupled feed method, a rectangular microstrip patch employing a multilayer substrate structure was designed and built. The main motivation of this work was to develop large bandwidth antennas for the PCS band 1850-1990 MHz. The new prototype is characterized by a 10% bandwidth around the center frequency of 1.90 GHz and a low front to back ratio. To examine the performances, numerical results, measurements of S-parameters and radiation patterns are presented.

articleTitle: Design and producibility optimization of single-bias d.c. coupled 10 Gbit/s MMIC transimpedance amplifiers using a GaAs enhancement/depletion PHEMT technology
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The design, fully market driven, is described of a d.c. coupled monolithic amplifier for 10 Gbit/s optical communications with 8.7 GHz operational bandwidth, 58 dB/spl Omega/ transimpedance gain and equivalent input noise current density lower than 6 pA//spl radic/Hz. The paper also discusses some important design issues on cost and producibility optimization of the circuit, which makes use of an original mixed inductive and capacitive peaking technique and of an advanced 0.2 /spl mu/m gate length enhancement-depletion GaAs HEMT technology.

articleTitle: Simulation of optical receivers with direct detection
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The results of a simulation study on the performance of optical receivers for direct-detection systems is presented. The variation of the bit error rate as a function of the received optical power for different transmission bit rates was used as criteria to analyze the receiver performance under different pre-amplification cases.

articleTitle: Diversity-combining analysis in a Nakagami environment
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper investigates the use of diversity in an environment where the signal is assumed to follow the Nakagami-m fading statistics. The diversity branches are considered to be uncorrelated and the signals arrive at the branches having the same mean value and the same fading parameter (m) Analytical formulations are presented for the widely known combining techniques with closed-form formulas been accomplished for most of the cases. The investigations carried out here serve the purpose of yielding a more general solution to the diversity-combining problem.

articleTitle: Experimental results for quartz ST 300/spl deg/ versus quartz ST 25/spl deg/
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This work presents experimental results comparing quartz ST 300/spl deg/ Natural Single Phase Unidirectional Transducer (NSPUDT) orientation (Euler angles: 0/spl deg/ 132.75/spl deg/ 300/spl deg/) with quartz ST 25/spl deg/ NSPUDT orientation (Euler angles: 0/spl deg/ 132.75/spl deg/ 25/spl deg/). The well-known quartz ST 25/spl deg/ is a largely used Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) orientation for low loss, high performance consumer and communication SAW filters, required in modern wireless communication, and remote control equipment. A method of searching for NSPUDT orientations, devised by one of the authors in a previous publication, suggested that quartz ST 300/spl deg/ should have better directivity behavior, thus improved NSPUDT performance. The experimental results herein reported verify that the quartz ST 300/spl deg/ presents much higher directivity with respect to the 25/spl deg/ orientation, thus confirming with remarkable agreement previous theoretical predictions done by one of the authors.

articleTitle: Propagation loss within buildings
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Along the last years, an increasing demand for mobile radio systems operating within buildings has been observed. Considering the complex structure of a building, an important problem for planning such systems is the prediction of propagation loss. An empirical prediction model to be used in the frequency range from 0.8 to 2.0 GHz is proposed in this paper. The basic parameters of this model were fixed in using a reasonable large data bank established from measurements published in the open literature. The model is quite simple and, in spite of its limitations, appears to be a powerful tool for planning indoor systems.

articleTitle: Distributed gain and spectral gain-saturation effects in erbium doped fibers
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Distributed gain and spectral gain-saturation effects of erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) were measured using a coherent reflectrometry technique. We find that the spectral performance can be improved if the gain needs are relaxed. A hole in the spectral dependence of the gain depletion was also observed, which could be related to the Spectral Hole Burning (SHB) phenomenon.

articleTitle: Analysis of a x-cut Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ electrooptic modulator with a ridge structure
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: An analysis of a Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder traveling-wave electrooptic modulator with a ridge structure is presented in this work. The performance of the device is studied assuming x-cut substrate. Two configurations employing ridge structure are compared to a conventional one. This work also presents the influence of some fabrication parameters of the optical waveguide on the factors which evaluates the efficiency of the modulators. The characteristics of both the optical waveguide and the coplanar waveguide electrode are computed applying the scalar finite element method.

articleTitle: A new technique for obtaining medium current erbium ion beams, for photonics devices, using typical microelectronics ion implanter
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The technique described here is intended to produce Er/sup ++/ beams, using typical ion implanter equipment normally used for microelectronics application. Erbium is a fundamental species whose incorporation into optical/semiconductor substrates produces stimulated radiation that allows the fabrication of photonics devices. The erbium ion implantation in contrast to the fiber diffusion process has all the inherent advantages of ion implantation i.e., high doses, vertical profiles, low thermal process among others. This technique uses the same ion source of the original equipment (Freeman type) and focuses on the placement of the erbium material in the arc chamber. Currents up to 100 /spl mu/A were obtained, which implies that doses up to 10/sup 17/ cm/sup -2/ could be reached. Double ionized atoms of erbium are produced by a plasma enhanced sputtering process and accelerated with a voltage up to 200 kV reaching beams close to 400 keV.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic imaging by the genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The genetic algorithm is used to reconstruct the shapes of two perfectly conducting cylinders. Based on the boundary condition and the measured scattered field, a set of nonlinear integral equations is derived and the imaging problem is reformulated into an optimization problem. The genetic algorithm is then employed to find the global extreme solution of the cost function. Numerical examples are given to demonstrate the capability of the inverse algorithm. Good reconstruction is obtained even when the multiple scattering between two conductors is serious. In addition, the effect of Gaussian noise on the reconstruction results is investigated.

articleTitle: Modulational instability in multiamplified optical systems with dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The advent of optical amplifiers made possible repeaterless optical fibre links of thousands of kilometres. An important limiting factor in achieving such distances is the interaction between ASE noise, generated by optical amplification, and the co-propagating signal, consisting of the phenomena of modulational instability and side-band instability. This paper describes briefly the modelling of these phenomena and, through numerical simulations, verifies the influence of modulational instability on the choice of parameters such as power level, fibre group-velocity dispersion and dispersion compensation methods, allowing conclusions with direct application to the design of optical communication systems.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of tellurite-based optical fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A numerical analysis for erbium-doped tellurite-based fiber amplifiers (EDFA) is presented for the first time in the literature. Modal and propagation equations are solved using the finite element method and a Runge-Kutta algorithm, respectively, and applied to a homogeneous four level erbium-doped fiber pumped at 1480 nm. Energy transfer due to cooperative up-conversion, cross relaxation and excited state absorption is considered. Comparisons with published experimental data confirm the present theoretical results.

articleTitle: Impact of stimulated Raman scattering on the transmission performance of WDM systems
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: We show that there is a trade-off between stimulated Raman scattering and other optical nonlinearities that can be used to improve system performance.

articleTitle: High power microwave applications in particle accelerators
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Particle accelerators are the world largest users of microwave power. These facilities have been historically the test ground for new ideas and equipment involving high power microwaves. New accelerators are been planned which will require hundreds of MW of microwave power. For these, new CW and pulsed klystron amplifiers are being design and tested spanning a frequency spectrum from 300 MHz up to 14 GHz and pick power up to 150 MW. Many of the proposed projects rely on the development of new microwave systems that are on the frontier of known technology. In this paper the author discusses a few of the characteristics of the high power microwave systems used in particle accelerators, in an attempt to offer a glimpse in the huge universe of problems addressed to by this area of research and development.

articleTitle: Analysis of frequency selective surfaces on uniaxial anisotropic substrates
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The scattering of electromagnetic waves from frequency selective surfaces (FSS) on anisotropic substrates is investigated, by using a full-wave analysis. The reflection and transmission coefficients are determined for FSS comprised of conducting patches on a uniaxial anisotropic layer, as function of the geometry parameters and of the dielectric anisotropy.

articleTitle: Multi-energy arsenic-ion-implanted GaAs photoconductive switches for ultrafast and millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: GaAs bombarded with arsenic ions at multiple dosages with various implantation energies were used to fabricate ultrafast photoconductive switches with picosecond response and bandwidth exceeding 500 MHz.

articleTitle: Novel cylindrical finite-difference time-domain schemes for transient electromagnetic simulations in unbounded, dispersive regions
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Three-dimensional (3-D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) schemes for transient simulation of electromagnetic wave propagation in complex (inhomogeneous, dispersive and conductive) media and cylindrical coordinates are presented. The schemes incorporate an extension of the perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition (ABC) to 3-D cylindrical coordinates. Dispersion in the media is incorporated through the use of piecewise-linear recursive convolution (PLRC). Numerical simulation results are included.

articleTitle: A prelude to the modelling of the dynamic properties of attenuation on slant-path links
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: In this paper, the statistics of the number and duration of fades-within specific duration ranges-on five slant path links in Brazil are presented and discussed. This duration scaling seeks to identify the contributions from dynamically different types of rain, such as convective and stratiform, which combine to form an overall cumulative distribution of rainfall. By identifying the range of influence of each rainfall regime it will be easier to build an accurate statistical model for the dynamics of attenuation.

articleTitle: Parametric model of a class C tube amplifier for industrial r.f. applications
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: This paper presents a parametric model of a triode which introduces seven parameters. It allows calculation of the a.c. and d.c. electrical variables of a class C amplifier from the d.c. anode and grid bias voltages, the load impedance and the a.c. exciting signal. This model can be used for designing the input and the output circuits and for optimizing the performance of the amplifier by choosing the best bias conditions.

articleTitle: 4/spl times/2.5 Gb/s transmission over standard singlemode fiber with amplifier spacing of 160 km
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A 4/spl times/2.5 Gb/s WDM transmission system was demonstrated over 740 km of standard singlemode fiber with amplifier spacing of 160 km. The four line amplifiers used have saturated output power of 12 dBm and non-equalized gain profile. To the authors' knowledge, this is the largest repeater spacing demonstrated for a WDM system without ASE filtering. Bit error rates as low as 10/sup -16/ were measured for received power ranging between -30 and -27 dBm, depending on the channel. The power penalties are below 2 dB for a bit error rate of 10/sup -9/. This penalty is mainly due to accumulated noise from the amplifiers.

articleTitle: New fast efficient technique for solving electromagnetic eigenvalue problems for multiconductor and multilayer planar transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: A full-wave electromagnetic technique is developed for the rapid and accurate calculation of the dispersion characteristics in multiconductor and multilayer planar transmission lines. The proposed method is based on the Mrozowski and Przybyszewski algorithms. This powerful method calculates an approximate value of propagation constant at a desired frequency based on more accurate computations of the field distribution and propagation constant at a few selected frequency points. Comparison with previously accurate published data and numerical tests are first performed to confirm the accuracy of our procedure. Numerical results for several configurations are presented.

articleTitle: DWDM transmission in high capacity optical systems using large effective area NZ-DSF LEAF fiber
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: System test results obtained with large effective area NZ-DSF LEAFO fiber are reviewed and the impact of optimization of some parameters on the performance of long-haul DWDM systems is discussed. The performance of LEAF fiber in different system configurations is also presented. In all studied cases, the benefit of the large effective area of the fiber is confirmed by the measurements of reduced nonlinear fiber-induced penalty.

articleTitle: An investigation into the non-thermal biological effects and medical applications of microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: Thirty years ago, Herbert Frohlich postulated that extremely weak microwave signals may act as a trigger for certain bioeffects. To be able to demonstrate a clear correlation between coherent oscillations and biological processes would have extremely important implications for medical research. For example, a technology could be developed to permit the detection of abnormal cells very much earlier than is currently possible, long before any clinical/chemical signs of malignancy were present, if it is thought that there may be an "electromagnetic trigger" that switches on the resulting chemical interaction between cells. If this trigger mechanism can be identified and measured, it may be possible to stop any subsequent interaction between cells and "follow-on" chemical phase resulting in cancerous cells.

articleTitle: Biological effects of microwave and RF
publicationTitle: 1999 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference
abstract: The relevant microwave and radio frequency (MW/RF) radiation biological effects are reviewed. Thermal and non-thermal effects due to electromagnetic field absorption in body tissues are considered. Numerical simulation and available guidelines for safety levels are discussed. The scenario in Brazil is briefly described, particularly regarding cellular base station measurements and simulation of the interaction of a handheld phone with a human head.
